tags.name: Properties
tags.description: Manage Properties — the physical premises you sell: hotels, motels, lodges, cabins, chalets, apartments and the like. Each property has its own address and details, so create one property per premises rather than combining several into a single entry.

tags.name: Room Types
tags.description: Manage Room Types — the accommodation inventory (rooms, villas, dormitory beds) of a Property.

tags.name: Rate Plans
tags.description: Manage Rate Plans — pricing plans of how to sell Room Types: prices per occupancy, rate derivation rules, and per-weekday restriction defaults.

tags.name: Photos
tags.description: Upload and manage Property and RoomType photos.

tags.name: Taxes
tags.description: Manage Taxes — individual charges (VAT, city tax, fees) applicable to a Rate Plan or Property. Taxes reach a Rate Plan grouped in a Tax Set.

tags.name: Tax Sets
tags.description: Manage Tax Sets — named groups of Taxes applied to Rate Plans, with the order the taxes are calculated in. The first set of a Property becomes its default and is applied to every new Rate Plan of the Property automatically; a Rate Plan detached from a set falls back to it. See `default_tax_set_id` on Properties and `tax_set_id` on Rate Plans.

tags.name: Hotel Policies
tags.description: Manage Hotel Policies — general property rules: check-in/out windows, guest limits, internet, parking, pets, and smoking. A policy belongs to one property, and the property points at it through `hotel_policy_id` (see the Properties resource); deleting the policy clears that reference.

tags.name: ARI
tags.description: Read and update Availability, Rates and Inventory. Rates and restrictions are held per Rate Plan and date; real availability is held per Room Type and date, and every Rate Plan of that Room Type reads it back as its own `availability`. Updates on both paths are queued: the response references a background task per Property (see the Tasks resource), and the new values are readable a moment later rather than at once. The `availability_offset` and `max_availability` values a read returns are set through Channel Availability Rules, not here.

tags.name: Channel Availability Rules
tags.description:
Availability overrides (stop-sales, offsets, caps) for specific Room Types and
Channels over a date range — closing out a channel for a holiday week, or capping
what one Room Type publishes to one Channel.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Read-only log of asynchronous tasks processed for a Property (channel syncs, scheduled updates), with timing and outcome.

tags.name: Facilities
tags.description:
Read-only dictionary of property- and room-type-level facilities (amenities).
Channex maintains both dictionaries; they cannot be added to through the API.
Contact Channex to have a missing facility added.

tags.name: Reference Data
tags.description: Static reference lists: time zones and supported currencies.

tags.name: Bookings
tags.description: Bookings received from the connected channels, together with the revisions they are built from. A booking is the current state of a reservation — the latest of its revisions; a revision is one parsed and normalised message from a booking source. Read bookings and their revisions, pull the feed of revisions not yet acknowledged, acknowledge what you received, and inspect the raw source message a revision was parsed from. To keep a PMS in step, pull the feed rather than polling the booking list; either source works for the initial pull.

tags.name: Booking CRS
tags.description: Creating and updating bookings from your own system rather than receiving them from a channel, including bookings that originated at an OTA. Requires the Booking CRS application installed on the Property; the API is in beta and may change.

tags.name: Booking Reporting
tags.description: Reports sent back to the OTA about what happened with a booking: a guest no-show, invalid credit card details, a cancellation caused by them, a change of stay, and guest misconduct. Supported for Booking.com bookings; no-shows for Expedia as well.

tags.name: Booking Payouts
tags.description: What Booking.com pays out for a booking: the payout details, the price breakdown behind them, and the bank transfer payout. Available for bookings that came through a Booking.com channel.

tags.name: Booking Payments
tags.description: Payments of a booking: list them and process charges, pre-authorizations, settlements, voids, and refunds. Requires the Payments application installed on the Property; without it every operation here answers `403 Forbidden`.

tags.name: Booking Messages
tags.description: Chat with guests at the booking level: read and send the messages of a booking, and fetch them from the channel on demand. Requires the Messages & Reviews application installed on the Property.

tags.name: Groups
tags.description: Manage Groups — sets of Properties you manage together, and the users who may reach them. Every Property belongs to at least one Group and may belong to several; a Group that still holds a Property cannot be deleted.

tags.name: Group Users
tags.description: Manage Group Users — a user's membership of a Group, which grants them access to every Property in it. A membership carries a role and, optionally, access policy overrides on top of it.

tags.name: Property Users
tags.description: Manage Property Users — a user's access to a single Property. An access carries a role and, optionally, access policy overrides on top of it, and ownership can be handed to another user.

tags.name: Live Feed
tags.description:
Feed of notable account events (new bookings, synchronization errors, guest requests): list and read them, and resolve actionable guest requests.

Airbnb inquiries, reservation requests and alteration requests wait for a decision. Each arrives as a live feed event of the same kind — also delivered as a webhook of that name (see the Webhooks resource) — and is answered with `POST /live_feed/{id}/resolve`. An inquiry also appears as a system message in the guest's message thread, whose `meta.live_feed_event_id` names the event to resolve (see the Message Threads resource).

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Push notifications for what happens on an account. A webhook subscribes a callback URL
to a set of events; when one occurs, Channex sends it a `POST` request.

A webhook watches one property, or — created with `property_id: null` — every property
of a billing account. A new webhook is inactive until `is_active` is set.

## What is delivered

Every delivery is a `POST` to `callback_url` with a JSON body of five keys:

- `event` — the event name, one of the values `/webhooks/events` lists.
- `property_id` — the property the event happened on.
- `user_id` — the user who caused it, or `null` for events the platform raises itself,
  which is most of them. Useful for ignoring changes your own integration made.
- `timestamp` — when the event happened, ISO 8601 UTC with microseconds, e.g.
  `2026-09-21T13:58:55.587742Z`.
- `payload` — the event's own data. Present only when the webhook's `send_data` is
  true; when it is false the key is absent altogether and the other four are all the
  delivery carries.

A signed webhook carries three `x-hmac-*` headers besides. See the Webhook Signing Keys
resource for what they hold and how to verify them — the `x-hmac-timestamp` header is
Unix seconds, not the body's `timestamp`.

## Retries

A delivery is successful when the callback URL answers `2xx`. A `5xx`, a connection
refused, a DNS failure, a timeout (30 seconds to connect, 30 to read) or a TLS error is
retried; a `4xx`, a redirect — which is never followed — and an expired TLS certificate
are final and are not.

There are eleven retries after the first attempt, spaced 1 minute, 2, 4, 8, 15, 30
minutes, then 1, 2, 4, 6 and 10 hours, so the last one lands about 24 hours after the
event. Those gaps are the earliest a retry is made, not the exact moment: a retry can
run up to a minute later.

Deliveries to one host are made one at a time, so a slow endpoint delays its own queue.
A webhook whose oldest unresolved failure is 72 hours old is deactivated — `is_active`
becomes false, the account is notified by email, and the pending deliveries for that
host are dropped. A `4xx` starts that clock as surely as a `5xx` does.

## Order

Deliveries are not ordered: a delivery retried after a failure arrives after ones raised
later, so a payload can describe a state older than the one before it. Treat a delivery
as a signal that something changed rather than as the change itself, and read the
current state back through the API — `GET /booking_revisions/{id}` for a booking event,
the availability and restrictions endpoints for an `ari` one.

tags.name: Webhook Signing Keys
tags.description:
HMAC keys that sign webhook deliveries, so that a receiving endpoint can tell that a
callback came from Channex and that its body was not altered on the way.

A key is a shared secret: Channex holds it and so do you. It is not an API credential
— it authenticates nothing against this API and grants no access. It is used in one
direction only, on the callbacks Channex sends to you.

A key belongs to a billing account and holds up to two secret versions — the current
one plus an optional pending one, which is what makes rotation zero-downtime. To turn
signing on, point a webhook at the key with `signing_key_id` and set `is_signed`.

## What is signed

Every delivery of a signed webhook — the `POST` Channex makes to the webhook's
`callback_url` — carries three headers:

- `x-hmac-timestamp` — Unix timestamp (seconds) taken when the delivery was signed.
- `x-hmac-signature-256` — comma-separated lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256 signatures, one
  per secret version of the key, the current version first.
- `x-hmac-keys-256` — comma-separated version labels (`...` followed by each secret's
  last 6 characters), in the same order as the signatures.

Each signature is computed over the string `{timestamp}.{raw request body}`: the value
of `x-hmac-timestamp`, a dot, and the exact bytes of that delivery's body. Nothing else
enters it — neither the callback URL nor the webhook's `request_params` and `headers`.

## Verifying a delivery

Recompute HMAC-SHA256 over `{timestamp}.{raw body}` with your stored secret, then
compare it against the signature at the position whose label in `x-hmac-keys-256` ends
with your secret's last 6 characters.

## Rotating a key

`generate` adds a pending secret version beside the current one, and deliveries are
then signed with both — so verification against the current secret keeps working while
the new secret is stored on your side. `rotate` promotes the newest version to be the
sole current version, after which deliveries carry its signature alone.

post.description:
Resolve an actionable live feed event: answer the guest request it carries.
Applicable to `reservation_request`, `alteration_request`, and `inquiry`
events; other event kinds are rejected with `422 not_supported`.

The shape of `resolution` depends on the kind of the event:

| Event kind            | Decision             | `resolution`                                           |
| --------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `reservation_request` | Accept               | `{"accept": true}`                                     |
| `reservation_request` | Decline              | `{"accept": false, "reason": "dates_not_available"}`   |
| `inquiry`             | Pre-approve          | `{"type": "preapproval"}`                              |
| `inquiry`             | Send a special offer | `{"type": "special_offer", "total_price": 450}`        |
| `alteration_request`  | Accept               | `{"accept": "accept"}`                                 |
| `alteration_request`  | Decline              | `{"accept": "decline"}`                                |
| `alteration_request`  | Withdraw             | `{"accept": "cancel"}`                                 |

`accept` is a boolean for reservation requests and a string for alteration
requests, and an inquiry is answered with `type` rather than `accept`.
Fields that belong to another event kind are ignored.

A decision is final: resolving an already-resolved event returns it
unchanged. Returns the event with its `payload` updated with the
resolution outcome.

Update rates and restrictions for specific Rate Plans and dates. Each change
object carries the Property and the Rate Plan it applies to, and targets
either a single `date` or the range `date_from`–`date_to`, optionally
narrowed to specific `days`. Sending both a `date` and the pair is refused,
and so is sending neither.

reference per Property, and the new values are readable a moment later rather
than at once. See the Tasks resource to follow a task to completion.

Change objects are applied in the order given, so a broad range can be set
first and overridden by later, narrower objects.

A change object that fails validation is rejected on its own and reported
under `meta.warnings` while the others are still applied — such a response is
still `200 OK`, and `data` is empty only when every change object was
rejected. A range that starts in the past is clamped to today rather than
rejected, and the clamp is reported as a warning of its own.

Rate limited to ten requests a minute per Property. Availability updates
carry a limit of ten a minute of their own, so twenty ARI updates a minute
per Property in all; beyond that the request answers `429 Too Many
Requests`, and nothing is applied until the limit expires.

Generate a new secret version for the key.

The new version is created pending, not current, so consumers keep verifying against
the current secret — deliveries are signed with both until the key is rotated.

post.description:
Rotate the key: promote the pending secret version to be the sole current version and
retire the others. Afterwards deliveries are signed with the promoted secret only, so
switch verification to it — announced by its masked label in the `x-hmac-keys-256`
header — before rotating. No new secret is created and none is revealed: the response
masks the version secrets. A successful rotation stamps the
key's `rotated_at`. A key with no pending version cannot be rotated — generate one
first.

Answer to an `alteration_request` event: a guest's request to change a
confirmed booking.

cancelling emits nothing — read the event again to confirm the stored
outcome. The guest can also withdraw the request on Airbnb before it is

LiveFeed.LiveFeedReservationRequestResol.description:
Answer to a `reservation_request` event: accept or decline a guest's request
to book. Airbnb holds the requested dates for 24 hours while the request
awaits an answer.

Accepting charges the guest's payment method; if the charge fails, the guest
has 24 hours to update it before the request is voided. Accepting emits the
`accepted_reservation` webhook at once; the booking itself arrives later as a
`booking_new` event, once Airbnb confirms the stay.

Declining emits the `declined_reservation` webhook, and no booking is
created. Declining with `dates_not_available`, or leaving the request
unanswered, keeps the requested dates blocked on Airbnb until they are made
available again.

RatePlans.DerivedOption.description:
Rules deriving values from the Parent Rate Plan or from the primary occupancy option, keyed by the restriction they modify.

The object is keyed by the restriction a rule list modifies — `rate`, `min_stay_arrival`, `min_stay_through` or `stop_sell` — and each key holds a list of `[operation, value]` rules. `null` or `[]` in place of the object means no derived option. A key outside these four is refused unless its value is empty.

`rate` takes any number of rules, applied to the original value in order, from left to right:

- `increase_by_amount` — add the amount
- `increase_by_percent` — increase by the percent
- `decrease_by_amount` — subtract the amount
- `decrease_by_percent` — decrease by the percent

The value is the amount or the percent as a string, for example `"10"` or `"5.00"`; a decimal comma is accepted. It must not be negative. `decrease_by_percent` must stay below 100 once rounded to two decimals — `"99.99"` is accepted, `"99.995"` is not; `increase_by_percent` has no upper limit. For an original rate of 100.00:

```json
{"rate": [["increase_by_percent", "5.00"], ["increase_by_amount", "12.00"]]}
```

100.00 + 5% = 105.00, then 105.00 + 12.00 = 117.00. An empty list, `{"rate": []}`, derives the rate unchanged.

`min_stay_arrival` and `min_stay_through` take one rule at most, `["set", <positive integer>]`, and `stop_sell` one rule at most, `["set", <boolean>]`: the restriction takes the given value instead of the original one.

derived_option.description:
Rules deriving this option's values from the Parent Rate Plan or the primary occupancy option, keyed by the restriction they modify. Defaults to `{"rate": []}`, derive the rate unchanged, when the rate plan has a parent.

The object is keyed by the restriction a rule list modifies — `rate`, `min_stay_arrival`, `min_stay_through` or `stop_sell` — and each key holds a list of `[operation, value]` rules. `null` or `[]` in place of the object means no derived option. A key outside these four is refused unless its value is empty.

`rate` takes any number of rules, applied to the original value in order, from left to right:

- `increase_by_amount` — add the amount
- `increase_by_percent` — increase by the percent
- `decrease_by_amount` — subtract the amount
- `decrease_by_percent` — decrease by the percent

The value is the amount or the percent as a string, for example `"10"` or `"5.00"`; a decimal comma is accepted. It must not be negative. `decrease_by_percent` must stay below 100 once rounded to two decimals — `"99.99"` is accepted, `"99.995"` is not; `increase_by_percent` has no upper limit. For an original rate of 100.00:

```json
{"rate": [["increase_by_percent", "5.00"], ["increase_by_amount", "12.00"]]}
```

100.00 + 5% = 105.00, then 105.00 + 12.00 = 117.00. An empty list, `{"rate": []}`, derives the rate unchanged.

`min_stay_arrival` and `min_stay_through` take one rule at most, `["set", <positive integer>]`, and `stop_sell` one rule at most, `["set", <boolean>]`: the restriction takes the given value instead of the original one.

An invalid derived option is refused with `422` `validation_error`. Each problem is reported under its own key in `details`, and one request can return several keys:

```
<prefix>.<restriction>[.<rule index>[.<element index>]]
```

`<restriction>` is the key as sent, for example `rate`. `<rule index>` is the 0-based position of the rule in the list as sent; `null` and `[]` entries are skipped but keep their position. `<element index>` is `0` for the operation and `1` for the value. When the operation is wrong, the value of that rule is not checked.

| Condition | Key | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A key outside the four restrictions, with a non-empty value | `<prefix>.ratee` | `unknown restriction` |
| The value of a key is not a list | `<prefix>.rate` | `must be a list` |
| An entry of the list is not a list | `<prefix>.rate` | `must be a list of [operation, value] rules` |
| More than one rule for `min_stay_arrival`, `min_stay_through` or `stop_sell` | `<prefix>.min_stay_through` | `must hold at most one rule` |
| A rule is not a two-item list | `<prefix>.rate.0` | `must be an [operation, value] pair` |
| An unknown operation, or one the restriction does not take | `<prefix>.rate.0.0` | `incorrect derived_option rule` |
| A `rate` value that is not a number | `<prefix>.rate.0.1` | `amount must be a number` |
| A negative `rate` value | `<prefix>.rate.0.1` | `amount must not be negative` |
| A `decrease_by_percent` value of 100 or more | `<prefix>.rate.0.1` | `percent must be less than 100` |
| A `min_stay_arrival` or `min_stay_through` value that is not a positive integer | `<prefix>.min_stay_arrival.0.1` | `must be a positive integer` |
| A `stop_sell` value that is not a boolean | `<prefix>.stop_sell.0.1` | `must be a boolean` |

For the options of a rate plan, `<prefix>` is `options.derived_option`, without the position of the option: `options.derived_option.rate.0.1`.

Occupancy options. A `per_room` rate plan takes one option for the maximum occupancy; a `per_person` rate plan takes an option per possible count of adult guests. The set of options is fixed at creation: an update can change them but not add or remove one.

Exactly one option has `is_primary: true`, whatever the `rate_mode` (`cascade` included); no primary option, or more than one, is refused with `422` (`details.options: ["should have exactly one primary option"]`). Each occupancy appears once — `2` and `"2"` count as the same value; a repeated occupancy is refused with `422` (`details.options: ["occupancy 2 is duplicated"]`, several values sorted and joined: `"occupancy 1, 2 is duplicated"`). An `occupancy` that is neither an integer nor a string that parses as one (for example `"five"`) is refused with `422` (`details.options: ["occupancy is invalid"]`).

The options are validated as a whole: an invalid option, primary or not, fails the request and nothing is created. The response carries every option created.

Restrictions.AvailabilityDocument.description:
Answer of the Get Availability method: each key is a Room Type id, each Room
Type maps dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) to the number of rooms available to sell on
that date. The number can be negative. A Property the caller cannot reach
yields an empty document.

date.description: Single date the change applies to. Give either this or the `date_from`–`date_to` pair, never both.

date_to.description: End of the applicable date range. Required together with `date_from` when `date` is not given.

days.description: Days of the week to affect within `date_from`–`date_to`; omitted means every day. Ignored when a single `date` is given.

availability.description: Number of rooms available to sell. A whole number, zero or more.

Restrictions.RateValue.description:
A rate value. Two forms are accepted: a decimal amount written as a string
(`"200.00"`), or an integer in the minimum fraction of the currency (`20000`
for 200.00 USD). Both avoid floating-point issues, and a bare fractional
number is refused. Must be greater than 0.

Restrictions.RestrictionKind.description:
A value that can be read back for a Rate Plan and date.
`availability` — rooms left to sell, derived from the Room Type.
`availability_offset` — amount subtracted from the Room Type availability before it is published.
`closed_to_arrival` — a stay may not begin on the date.
`closed_to_departure` — a stay may not end on the date.
`max_availability` — ceiling on published availability, or `null` for none.
`max_sell` — maximum rooms that may be sold on the date, or `null` for no limit.
`max_stay` — maximum nights a stay may run; `0` means no maximum.
`min_stay_arrival` — minimum nights a stay arriving on the date must run.
`min_stay_through` — minimum nights a stay covering the date must run.
`rate` — the price for the date.
`stop_sell` — whether the date is closed for sale.
`stop_sell_manual` — whether the date is closed because it was closed explicitly, rather than because its availability or rate is 0.

date_to.description: End of the applicable date range. Past dates are refused. Required together with `date_from` when `date` is not given.

Rate for the date. Must be greater than 0 and within the Property's price

`both` refuses it — send the specific restriction instead.

Whether to close the date for sale. `0` and `1` are accepted as boolean
representations. A date whose availability or rate is 0 stays closed even
when this is `false`.

this API. `false` for a webhook you create yourself.

callback_url.description: URL called via POST when a subscribed trigger event occurs. Must carry a scheme and a resolvable host.

request_params.description: Additional GET query parameters appended to the callback request, or null when none are set.

Custom request headers for the callback request, or null when none are set. Use this
to authenticate against a protected endpoint, e.g.
`{ "Authorization": "Basic user:password" }`.

is_active.description: Whether the webhook is active. Only active webhooks receive notifications. `false` by default.

send_data.description:
Whether to include event payload data in the callback. When `false`, the delivery
carries `event`, `property_id`, `user_id` and `timestamp` and no `payload`. `false`
by default.

is_global.description:
Whether the webhook receives events from every property of the billing account rather
than from one. `false` by default, and fixed after creation: a property-level webhook
cannot be converted to a global one.

A global and a property-level webhook can cover the same event. When they point at
different callback URLs both are delivered; when they point at the same one the
delivery is made once, with the property-level webhook's settings.

is_signed.description:
Whether deliveries are signed. When `true`, every callback request carries the
`x-hmac-timestamp`, `x-hmac-signature-256` and `x-hmac-keys-256` headers, computed
with the key referenced by `signing_key_id`. The Webhook Signing Keys resource
describes the signed string and how to verify a delivery. `false` by default.

signing_key_id.description:
UUID of the signing key deliveries are signed with, or null when none is assigned.
Required whenever `is_signed` is true; the key must belong to a billing account the
caller is a member of. Responses also expose the key, with its masked versions,
through the `signing_key` relationship.
